text:
This year Hindustan Unilever agreed to buy OZiva outright for about $90 million, and sold its stake in Wellbeing Nutrition to USV. Supply6 raised ₹48 crore in a round led by Unilever Ventures.

Big money is picking its winners in Indian supplements. I launched a supplement brand three weeks ago, so I've been thinking about what this means for us and for the people buying.

More Indians take supplements every year, and most of them still can't tell what's inside the jar. When we asked our 1,870 pre-bookers what got in the way, the line we heard most was simple: in a busy life you can't keep up with ten supplements.

So that's where we've put our chips. Two drink mixes, one for the morning and one for the night, in place of a shelf of jars. Every dose printed on the pack. A lab report for each of our 19 ingredients, with 293 checks so far and none failed.

Large companies are very good at distribution. A small brand can show its working, answer every DM, and change a formula when the evidence changes.

Three weeks in, 250 people have bought SILT and 10 have already come back for more. Small numbers, and I read every review myself.

If you work in consumer health, I'd like to hear your view. Does all this consolidation make the category more trustworthy, or less?

#preventivehealth #founderjourney
